_comment: Permission requests the owner sends (owner request 2026-10-28). Each is a letter the owner sends from their own mail client; the library never sends mail. verified: where the contact was found. Kept in the repo; the hourly manual sync copies this file and permissions.py into <vault>/_incoming/_manual/_permissions/ and runs it there.

requests.publisher: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University)
requests.verified: plato.stanford.edu/contact.html (2026-10-28); also postal: Metaphysics Research Lab, Cordura Hall Room 202, 210 Panama Street, Stanford, CA 94305-4115
requests.work: the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (the entries of the current edition)
requests.how: as one copy of the published HTML entries, refreshed at most quarterly from your quarterly archive editions

requests.verified: the copyright pages of Hesperian's books name permissions@hesperian.org for any digital format (2026-10-28)
requests.work: Hesperian's health guides in English (Where There Is No Doctor, Where Women Have No Doctor, Where There Is No Dentist and the other titles you publish as free PDFs)
requests.how: as the PDF editions you publish on hesperian.org

requests.verified: spherestandards.org/intellectual-property asks for written permission at info@spherestandards.org (2026-10-28)
requests.work: the Sphere Handbook (2018 edition, and later editions when published) and its companion standards you publish
requests.how: as the PDF editions you publish

requests.publisher: UK Ministry of Defence, Development, Concepts and Doctrine Centre (DCDC)
requests.verified: UNVERIFIED as current: named as the doctrine contact in JDP 1-05 (2022). The publications say release outside the MOD goes through Defence Intellectual Property Rights (DIPR); ask DCDC to forward if needed.
requests.work: the UK joint doctrine publications (JDPs and JDNs) that the MOD publishes openly on GOV.UK
requests.how: as the PDF files published on GOV.UK

requests.publisher: National Center for Home Food Preservation, University of Georgia
requests.verified: nchfp.uga.edu's contact page (a form; no email address published), 2026-10-28
requests.work: the National Center for Home Food Preservation's own guides and recipe pages on nchfp.uga.edu (the USDA guides themselves are public domain and need no permission)
requests.how: as the pages and PDF files on nchfp.uga.edu

requests.verified: contact+mirror@kiwix.org is the address Kiwix names for mirror matters (mirror READMEs, 2026-10-28)
requests.paths: the OPDS catalog and the .sha256/.meta4 files of the ZIMs (the ZIM files themselves come from your mirrors)
requests.pace: a few hundred requests a month: one catalog read a day and one checksum per new ZIM
requests.alternative: a checksum list (or the .sha256 files) published on the mirrors would serve just as well

requests.publisher: US National Library of Medicine, National Center for Biotechnology Information
requests.pace: one file at a time, about 1 MB/s, the daily PubMed update files and a quarterly PubChem and Bookshelf refresh
requests.alternative: if robots.txt is meant only for web crawlers and scripted bulk downloads of these folders are welcome, a line saying so would be enough

requests.publisher: National Institute of Building Sciences (Whole Building Design Guide)
requests.verified: wbdg@nibs.org is given for WBDG questions on nibs.org (2026-10-28)
requests.hosts: nibs-s3-wbdg3-production.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com (the bucket the UFC PDFs are served from)
requests.paths: the Unified Facilities Criteria and other federal criteria PDFs linked from wbdg.org
requests.pace: one file at a time, a few thousand files once, then only new or changed ones
requests.alternative: a bulk download of the UFC library would serve just as well

requests.paths: the current UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot release files and the ChEMBL release
requests.pace: a handful of files per release, one at a time
requests.alternative: if robots.txt is meant only for web crawlers and scripted release downloads are welcome, a line saying so would be enough

requests.verified: UNVERIFIED as current: listed as the COD contact in database directories (2026-10-28); check the COD home page first
requests.alternative: rsync or another bulk route would serve just as well

requests.publisher: International Committee of the Red Cross, Library
requests.verified: library@icrc.org on the ICRC Library page (2026-10-28)
requests.paths: the openly published ICRC books and reports
requests.pace: one request every few seconds, once, then only new publications
requests.alternative: a list of the PDF links would serve just as well

requests.verified: UNVERIFIED: api@lovdata.no is named for the API in a third-party module; check lovdata.no/info/api first

requests.paths: public reference documents (NUREG reports and the reading-room collections linked from www.nrc.gov)
requests.alternative: its bot protection refuses the library's fetcher after a few requests; an allowance for its user agent would be enough

requests.publisher: US Occupational Safety and Health Administration
requests.alternative: its bot protection refuses the library's fetcher; an allowance for its user agent would be enough

requests.verified: govinfo's contact page (2026-10-28); the API's own issues are also tracked at github.com/usgpo/api
requests.situation: since late October its requests to api.govinfo.gov stop at robots.txt: https://api.govinfo.gov/robots.txt answers with a server error (HTTP 500, "Oops, Something went wrong"), and the robots rules (RFC 9309) require a crawler to read an unreachable robots.txt as "disallow everything"
requests.paths: the collections and packages your API serves to registered api.data.gov keys (my key is registered)
requests.pace: within your published API rate limits, one request at a time
requests.alternative: serving a robots.txt at api.govinfo.gov (even an empty one, or a 404) would be enough; so would a short reply saying the API may be used as documented
